openDecisions.question: Person filter matching: case-sensitive exact (current behaviour) or case-insensitive?
openDecisions.specSays: 02_BACKEND_API.md:272 — 'Case-insensitive exact/normalized match за current project pattern.' It assumes the project already normalizes.
openDecisions.codeSays: There is no case-insensitive person pattern. loans.repository.ts:335 does `where.personName = person` (plain equality) and loans.service.ts:72 only collapses whitespace via normalizeSearch. Migration 20260812115219 line 5 states the uk-UA-x-icu collation is deterministic, so equality stays byte-exact. 02_BACKEND_API.md:441 itself admits 'Олена' and 'олена' may stay distinct.
options: Mirror the active pages: exact, case-sensitive equality on personName.
Case-insensitive: lower(person_name) = lower($1) in the history query only.
Case-insensitive everywhere (history + active list).
openDecisions.recommendation: Option 1 for this task. The person value always arrives from a backend-provided option (sidebar top-people or the people endpoint), so it round-trips byte-exact; option 2 would make the history and the active pages disagree on what 'Олена' means, and option 3 is the cross-cutting change the spec's own non-goals rule out.
openDecisions.answer: Option 1 — exact, case-sensitive person matching, same as the active loans pages.

openDecisions.question: How much of the history list query goes to raw SQL?
openDecisions.specSays: 02_BACKEND_API.md:268 and 00_CLAUDE_TASK.md:556 — 'якщо Prisma не виражає column-to-column comparison або duration sort, використати safe parameterized SQL за патернами репозиторію.'
openDecisions.codeSays: Confirmed necessary: the result filter needs (returned_at AT TIME ZONE 'UTC')::date vs expected_return_date and duration_desc needs returned_date - loan_date; Prisma expresses neither. The repo already has both halves of the pattern — parameterized Prisma.sql + Zod row parsing in loans.repository.ts:139-181, and ordered-ids-then-hydrate in books.repository.ts:930-950.
options: One raw SQL statement returns the ordered page of ids (plus a window count), then a single Prisma findMany with the book include hydrates them.
Prisma findMany for the simple sorts, raw SQL only for result-filtered or duration-sorted requests.
Raw SQL returning full rows, mapping columns by hand.
openDecisions.recommendation: Option 1. It keeps one code path (so a filter bug cannot exist in only half the sorts), keeps the cover/publisher include in Prisma so there is no N+1 and no hand-mapped column list, and matches an existing precedent in this repo. Option 2 doubles the WHERE logic; option 3 loses the include.
openDecisions.answer: Option 1 — one raw SQL statement returning ordered ids + count, then one Prisma findMany with the existing include to hydrate.

openDecisions.question: Is a separate GET /api/loans/history/:loanId worth it, or should the list item carry contact and note?
openDecisions.specSays: 02_BACKEND_API.md §18 mandates the detail endpoint; §5 line 139 says the list must not carry fields only the drawer needs.
openDecisions.codeSays: The delta is four fields (contact, note, createdAt, updatedAt). The list already fetches the full BookLoan row and its book include, so the data is in memory either way — the endpoint costs a round trip on drawer open but buys a clean refetch target after a correction.
options: Follow the spec: separate detail endpoint, drawer fetches on open.
Fatten the list item with contact and note, drop the detail endpoint, drawer renders from the row already in cache.
openDecisions.recommendation: Option 1. The correction flow (A4/W12) needs an authoritative single-loan refetch anyway, and the endpoint is also the security boundary the tests in 04_TESTS_ACCEPTANCE.md §15 assert (own active loan must 404). Option 2 saves one small request and then needs the endpoint back for the correction response.
openDecisions.answer: Option 1 — keep GET /api/loans/history/:loanId as a separate endpoint.

openDecisions.question: Which primitive backs the detail drawer?
openDecisions.codeSays: Two exist. Sheet is the established feature-level drill-down (apps/web/src/features/characters/components/character-details-sheet.tsx, plus six advanced-filter sheets). Drawer (vaul) is used in features only indirectly, through apps/web/src/components/ui/mobile-page-overview-panel.tsx.
options: Sheet — right-side panel on desktop, matching character-details-sheet.
Drawer — bottom sheet, matching the mobile overview panel.
Sheet on desktop, Drawer on mobile.
openDecisions.recommendation: Option 1. It is the only primitive used directly for a detail drill-down today, it already handles focus trap and Escape, and it responds well on mobile. Option 3 doubles the component for one screen size with no requirement behind it.

openDecisions.question: Numbered pagination with pageNumber in the URL, or the 'Показати ще' infinite pattern the loans pages just moved to?
openDecisions.specSays: 03_FRONTEND.md:104 lists pageNumber among the URL params; 04_TESTS_ACCEPTANCE.md:162 requires 'page reset after filter change'; 01_PRODUCT_UX.md:318 says 'список плоский + pagination'.
openDecisions.codeSays: Commit 74ef0b29 deliberately replaced the loans pager with a show-more button: use-loans-list.ts:14 is a useInfiniteQuery and loans-query.ts:17-22 has no pageNumber parser at all. Meanwhile apps/web/src/components/ui/pagination.tsx is alive in quotes, publishers and reading-history.
options: Numbered pagination with pageNumber in the URL, as the spec's params list implies.
useInfiniteQuery + 'Показати ще', consistent with the two sibling loans pages, no pageNumber param.
Infinite list for items, but keep pageNumber in the URL as a resume cursor.
openDecisions.recommendation: Option 2. History is a scan-and-scroll list like the active pages, and reintroducing a pager one page over from the button that just replaced it is a visible inconsistency in the same nav group. The backend stays paginated either way, so nothing in the API changes; the 'page reset' acceptance criterion becomes 'the infinite query resets to page 1 on filter change', which useInfiniteQuery does for free when the params-bearing key changes. Choose option 1 only if numbered pages are wanted back across the whole loans group.
openDecisions.answer: Option 2 — useInfiniteQuery plus a 'Показати ще' button, no pageNumber in the URL.
openDecisions.answeredBy: user (prior instruction: pagination replaced by a show-more button across the loans pages)

openDecisions.question: Add @@index([userId, status, returnedAt]) alongside the existing @@index([userId, status]), or replace it?
openDecisions.specSays: 00_CLAUDE_TASK.md:558 — 'додати/перевірити індекс для userId + status + returnedAt, якщо немає еквівалентного'; 02_BACKEND_API.md:577 — 'Не додавати дублюючий index без потреби.'
openDecisions.codeSays: schema.prisma:404 has @@index([userId, status]) (created as book_loans_user_id_status_idx in migration 20260723191344, line 41). It is a strict prefix of the proposed index, so Postgres can serve every query it serves from the wider one. Keeping both means a second index maintained on every loan write for no read benefit.
options: Replace: drop @@index([userId, status]), add @@index([userId, status, returnedAt]).
Keep both.
Add nothing — accept a sort on returned_at without index support.
openDecisions.recommendation: Option 1, which is what the spec's own 'no duplicate index' line asks for. The generated migration will contain exactly one legitimate DROP INDEX (book_loans_user_id_status_idx); every other DROP INDEX line in that file must be stripped before deploy per CLAUDE.md §6.
openDecisions.answer: Option 1 — replace @@index([userId, status]) with @@index([userId, status, returnedAt]); exactly one legitimate DROP INDEX in the migration, every other DROP INDEX line stripped before deploy.

openDecisions.question: Person filter UI: typeahead autocomplete or a plain select of all people?
openDecisions.specSays: 00_CLAUDE_TASK.md:194 says 'Autocomplete/dropdown'; 02_BACKEND_API.md:452 says search support on the people endpoint is optional ('Можна підтримати').
openDecisions.codeSays: The active loans toolbar has no person control at all — person is set only by clicking a sidebar top-person (loans-view.tsx:86). A cmdk Command primitive exists (apps/web/src/components/ui/command.tsx) and the repo has an infinite-scroll-in-cmdk helper, but wiring it is meaningfully more work than a Select.
options: Plain Select fed by the people endpoint (no search param used yet).
cmdk typeahead against the people endpoint's search param.
openDecisions.recommendation: Option 1 for the first cut, with the backend search param still implemented (R5) so the upgrade is UI-only. A personal library rarely has more than a few dozen lenders, and a Select keeps keyboard access and labelling trivial.
openDecisions.answer: Option 1 — plain Select in the UI, backend search param still implemented.

openDecisions.question: The four icon names the spec asks for do not exist in the registry. Map or extend?
openDecisions.specSays: 00_CLAUDE_TASK.md:539-544 asks for history, circle-check, clock / clock-alert, calendar, users; line 537 forbids new SVGs when a fitting icon exists.
openDecisions.codeSays: apps/web/src/components/icons/ui-icon.tsx:5-113 has book-copy, check-circle, clock, calendar, user, alert-triangle, chart. It has no 'history', no 'circle-check' (the name is check-circle), no 'clock-alert', and no plural 'users'.
options: Map onto existing names: history -> book-copy, circle-check -> check-circle, clock-alert -> clock (or alert-triangle for late), users -> user.
Add history / clock-alert / users to the UiIcon registry from lucide.
openDecisions.recommendation: Option 1. Every requested semantic already has a close match, which is exactly the case line 537 covers. Note that app-shell.tsx imports lucide icons directly for nav, so W2's sidebar icon is unaffected by this choice.
openDecisions.answer: Option 1 — map onto the existing UiIcon names, no new SVGs.

openDecisions.question: Two return paths leave remindToReturn=true on a completed loan. Fix inside this task?
openDecisions.specSays: 02_BACKEND_API.md:537 — 'переконайся, що return flow не залишає pending reminder для completed loan'. 00_CLAUDE_TASK.md:605 — 'Не роби unrelated refactor.'
openDecisions.codeSays: The primary return path clears them (books.repository.ts:505-513 sets remindBeforeDays: null, remindToReturn: false). The ownership-change path (books.repository.ts:1462-1466) and the bulk path (bulk-books.repository.ts:272-275) set only returnedAt + status. No reminder can actually fire, because reminder-candidates.repository.ts:13-19 requires status='active' AND returnedAt IS NULL — so this is stale data, not a live bug.
options: Leave both as they are; record the inconsistency.
Add the two-field clear to both paths (about four lines) and cover it with a test.
Backfill existing rows too, via the P1 migration.
openDecisions.recommendation: Option 2, minus the backfill. The spec asks you to verify this path, the fix is two data fields in files you are already reasoning about, and it stops the history detail from ever reporting a reminder on a closed loan. Option 3 adds a data migration nothing reads.
openDecisions.answer: Option 2 minus the backfill — fix both return paths in this task, with a test, no data backfill.

openDecisions.question: Timezone basis for the calendar returned date.
openDecisions.specSays: 00_CLAUDE_TASK.md:119 and 02_BACKEND_API.md:168 — 'Перевикористай чинну date/timezone normalization стратегію проєкту', without naming it.
openDecisions.codeSays: The project's strategy is UTC, hardcoded: apps/api/src/core/iso-date.ts:6 sets UTC_TIME_ZONE = 'UTC' and every conversion (toIsoDate:35, parseIsoDate:23, startOfUtcDay:27) goes through it. There is no per-user timezone anywhere in the loans path.
options: UTC, matching iso-date.ts and the existing loan overdue logic.
A per-user timezone, introducing a new user preference.
openDecisions.recommendation: Option 1, and state the consequence plainly: a book returned at 23:30 Kyiv time on the due date is stored as the next UTC day and will read as 'late by 1 day'. Active-loan overdue already carries the same skew (loan-ui-status.ts:35), so history stays consistent with the pages beside it. Fixing this is a project-wide timezone decision, not a history feature.
openDecisions.answer: Option 1 — UTC, consistent with core/iso-date.ts and active-loan overdue. Accepted consequence: a return at 23:30 Kyiv on the due date reads as late by one day.
